latency_measured_on_target_hw_quote: We evaluated our model implementing the Visual Studio code on our MSI GS66 laptop (MSI, Taipei, Taiwan), equipped with a CPU speed of 5.3 GHz, 64 GB of RAM, and 6 GPUs.
target_hardware_named_quote: Finally, our proposed model was implemented on Raspberry PI 3B+, as shown in Figure 9.
hyperparams_full_quote: We used the default YOLOv8 in all five models to train our dataset and show the result after 50,000 iterations in Table 4. In addition, image hue 0.1, saturation 1.5, and exposure 1.5 were used.
coder_notes: leakage_risk=high: 6,000 screened images are rotated 90/180/270 degrees to 24,000 and only THEN split 70/10/20, so rotated copies of the same image are guaranteed to appear in train and test; sources also include video. split_protocol coded random_resplit - the ratios are stated but the word 'random' is not used and no disjointness criterion is given. n_val/n_test coded not_reported because only percentages are given (10% test / 20% validation of 24,000), never integers; note also that the stated 10%/20% assignment is unusual (test smaller than validation). task: detection_bbox from the YOLOv8 object-detection framing, but the paper also describes a two-class fire/non-fire image labelling, so 'classification' is a defensible alternative - flag for adjudication. FPR included in metrics_reported on the strength of the 'false detection rate of 0.7%' figure only. deployment_level L1: the model is put on a Raspberry Pi 3B+ but no field deployment, timing or duration is reported, and the paper elsewhere states the approach is incompatible with edge devices. Reported numbers are internally inconsistent (97% vs 96.7% training / 97% testing accuracy in adjacent sentences).
